faq.a: DSCR is annual net operating income divided by annual debt payments. It shows how many times over your income covers your loan payments. Lenders usually want at least 1.25, meaning income covers payments 1.25 times over.

Max annual debt service is net operating income divided by DSCR. Max monthly payment is that divided by 12. Max loan amount is the present value of that monthly payment over the term at the monthly interest rate.
faq.q: How is the maximum loan worked out?

faq.a: Yes. Net operating income is often approximated with EBITDA for this kind of estimate, but lenders use their own definitions and may adjust income for owner pay, one-off items, and other factors, so their figure can differ from yours.
faq.q: Can I use EBITDA instead of net operating income?

faq.a: No. This is an estimate based on the DSCR rule alone. Lenders also check credit, collateral, cash flow history, and other factors, and the loan they offer can be lower than this maximum.
faq.q: Will a lender approve this exact amount?

sources: The DSCR definition and the 1.25 lender convention are the standard lending practice supplied with this build, checked November 2026. The loan math is the standard present value of an annuity formula, and all figures come from the numbers you enter.
